MINUTES
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  SEPTEMBER 10, 2019

A regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to order by
MAYOR MITCHELL at 7:05 p.m.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

Council Member Zerunyan led the Pledge of Allegiance.

ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

City Council Members Absent:  None

City Staff Present: City Manager Greg Grammer
  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis
  City Attorney Don Davis
  Director of Community Development & Public Works David Wahba
  Planning Manager Jeannie Naughton
  Community Services Supervisor Cynthia Morquecho
  Maintenance Superintendent Mike Goldsmith
  City Clerk Heidi Luce

Others Present:  Kathleen McGowan, McGowan Consulting

CEREMONIAL ITEMS

A.  PROCLAMATION: DECLARING  SEPTEMBER  2019  “CHILDHOOD  CANCER
  AWARENESS MONTH”

MAYOR MITCHELL presented a proclamation declaring September 2019 “Childhood Cancer
Awareness Month.”

CONSENT CALENDAR

  The following routine matters will be acted upon by one vote to approve with the majority consent of
  the City Council. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless good cause is shown
  by a member prior to the roll call vote. (Items removed for individual consideration will be voted on
  separately.)

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF requested that Item 5F (Salary Resolutions – Department Heads)
be removed for individual consideration.

There being no objection, MAYOR MITCHELL so ordered.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  1
SEPTEMBER 10, 2019
   MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN,

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL APPROVE CONSENT CALENDAR ITEMS A-E AND
  G-J AS PRESENTED BELOW.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

A.  READING OF ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS BY TITLE ONLY

  APPROVED.

B.  CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF AUGUST 13, 2019

  APPROVED.

C.  DEMANDS AND WARRANTS AUGUST AND SEPTEMBER 2019

  APPROVED WARRANTS 61827 THROUGH 61931 IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $187.051.40; AND SUPPLEMENTAL WARRANTS 080419 THROUGH 080519;
  090119 THROUGH 090219 IN THE AMOUNT OF $154,642.00 FOR A GRAND
  TOTAL AMOUNT OF $341,693.40 WITH PROPER AUDIT.

D.  SCHEDULE OF INVESTMENTS REPORT – JULY 2019

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

E.  REVENUE AND EXPENDITURE REPORT – JULY 2019

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

G.  TRAFFIC AND SAFETY COMMITTEE MINUTES OF AUGUST 14, 2019

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

H.  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MINUTES OF AUGUST 19, 2019

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

I.  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION/EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES OF
  AUGUST 20, 2019 (SPECIAL JOINT MEETING)

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

J.  PLANNING COMMISSION MINUTES OF SEPTEMBER 3, 2019

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
SEPTEMBER 10, 2019
 REMOVED FOR INDIVIDUAL CONSIDERATION:

F.  SALARY RESOLUTIONS – DEPARTMENT HEADS

  ADOPTED RESOLUTION NO. 2447 AUTHORIZING PARS BENEFIT FOR
  IDENTIFIED MANAGEMENT CLASSIFICATION EMPLOYEE GROUP FOR FY
  2019-20

  Recommendation: That the City Council adopt Resolution 2447 authorizing the PARS
  benefit for identified Management Classification employee group for FY 2019-20.

  COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF requested that staff provide an overview of the PARS benefit
  as compared to the CalPERS benefit to further the Council’s commitment to maintaining
  costs.

  Assistant City Manager Davis explained that the Public Agency Retirement System
  (PARS) benefit is a supplemental benefit program for which the City may authorize
  participation or withdraw at any time and does not have any future pension liability. She
  stated that this year’s contribution is proposed at 2.5% for management employees and
  authorized for FY 19-20 only at a total cost of $10,740 which is reflected in the adopted
  budget.

  In response to COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF, Assistant City Manager confirmed that this
  action does not commit the city to a long-term benefit commitment.

  COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF moved, seconded by, MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL ADOPT RESOLUTION NO. 2447 AUTHORIZING
  PARS BENEFIT FOR IDENTIFIED MANAGEMENT CLASSIFICATION
  EMPLOYEE GROUP FOR FY 2019-20

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan and Zuckerman

City Clerk Luce read the resolution by title only.

PUBLIC COMMENT / PUBLIC PRESENTATIONS

Angie Gilbride, California Water Service Company provided a construction update on the Palos
Verdes Peninsula Water Reliability Project.

Recognizing that it was not yet 7:30 p.m., MAYOR MITCHELL took New Business items 8A, 8B
and 8C out of order.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
SEPTEMBER 10, 2019
 NEW BUSINESS (TAKEN OUT OR ORDER)

A.  SANITARY SEWER MANAGEMENT PLAN (SSMP)

  Recommendation: That the City Council: 1) Certify the City’s updated SSMP; and 2)
  Direct the Community Development/Public Works Director to sign the SSMP and forward
  for signature by Los Angeles County Department of Public Works after which an
  electronic copy is to be uploaded to the State Water Resources Control Board CIWQS
  website as well as posted on the City’s website.

  Director of Community Development/Public Works Wahba provided a staff report (as per
  the agenda material).

  MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ noted that in the statistics section at the of the report the
  statistics for collection system by division level are from 2015 and inquired as to why the
  statistics are not from a more current year.

  Director Wahba responded that staff will research that matter.

  Kathleen McGowan, McGowan Consulting stated that the appendices were provided by
  the County and staff will check to be sure there was nothing left out before submitting the
  report.

  Brief discussion ensued concerning the portions of the City that are not currently
  connected to the sewer system and food waste.

  In response to COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF, Director Wahba confirmed that sewer fees
  are paid directly to the County through a property tax assessment.

  In response COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN’S inquiry, Director Wahba stated that in
  addition to being located under City streets, some sewer lines are located in bridle trails
  and in easements between homes.

  COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF moved, seconded by, MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL CERTIFY THE CITY’S UPDATED SSMP; AND
  DIRECT STAFF TO: SIGN THE SSMP; FORWARD TO LOS ANGELES COUNTY
  DEPARTMENT OF PUBLIC WORKS FOR SIGNATURE; UPLOAD TO THE
  CALIFORNIA STATE WATER RESOURCES CONTROL BOARD CIWQS
  WEBSITE AND POST TO THE CITY’S WEBSITE.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan and Zuckerman

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
SEPTEMBER 10, 2019
 B.  PUBLICLY AVAILABLE PAY SCHEDULE

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve a Publicly Available Pay Schedule for
  the 2019-20 fiscal year in accordance with California Public Employees; Retirement
  System (CalPERS) regulations.

  Assistant City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

  In response to COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF, Assistant City Manager Davis stated that this
  schedule is developed in accordance with the approved salary resolutions adopted by the
  City Council in June of each year authorizing the salary schedules for each classification
  of employees.

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by, MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL APPROVE THE PUBLICLY AVAILABLE PAY
  SCHEDULE FOR THE 2019-20 FISCAL YEAR IN ACCORDANCE WITH
  CALIFORNIA PUBLIC EMPLOYEES’ RETIREMENT SYSTEM (CALPERS)
  REGULATIONS.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

C.  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION ACTION ITEM: MOUNTED SHOOTING
  COMPETITION

  Recommendation: Based upon the review of the event information submitted and the
  demonstration by the California Desperados to host their Cowboy mounted shooting
  event at Ernie Howlett Park; and with consideration of the type of noise produced by the
  event, the Equestrian Committee and Park and Activities Commission recommend that
  the City Council deny the event request to host a mounted shooting event at Ernie Howlett
  Park.

  Community Services Supervisor Morquecho provided a staff report (as per the agenda
  material).

  Assistant City Manager Davis noted that additional correspondence related to this item
  were received via e-mail and those messages were forwarded to the City Council and
  placed on the dais. She summarized the correspondence as follows:

  Brenda Caropino, Event Organizer – providing further explanation and details about the
  event.

  Tim Zigrang, Planning Commissioner and Equestrian Committee Member – expressing
  support for the event.

  Vicki Shinn, Equestrian Committee – expressing opposition to the event.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  5
SEPTEMBER 10, 2019
   Assistant City Manager Davis noted that staff also inquired with the Sheriff’s Department
  regarding this type of event and the Sheriff’s Dept. is familiar with the activities and they
  do not have concerns about the event being held locally.

  In response to MAYOR MITCHELL, Community Services Supervisor Morquecho
  confirmed that this event is proposed to be an all-day event.

  COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF thanked Ms. Caropino for providing the demonstration at
  Ernie Howlett Park and provided an overview of the demonstration as summarized in the
  minutes of the joint meeting.

  In response to MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ, Community Services Supervisor
  Morquecho stated that there is no date currently proposed, but if the event is approved
  staff will ensure that the date does not conflict with other activities at the park.

  Brenda Caropino, Event Organizer addressed the City Council to provide further
  explanation about the organization and the proposed event.

  In response to COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN regarding expected attendance and
  other locations, Ms. Caropino stated that there would likely be approximately 35-40
  people attending this event and other local events are in Norco and Corona. She also
  stated that the organization prefers the facilities at Ernie Howlett over Empty Saddle Club.

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN suggested that the organizer consider a shorter
  duration demonstration project or a clinic rather than an all-day event.

  Discussion ensued concerning other options for this type of event. It was noted that there
  was a demonstration previously at the City Celebration several years ago and there is
  currently little participation in this event by the local equestrian community. Further
  discussion ensued concerning the safety/noise concerns associated with event.

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN moved, seconded by, MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL UPHOLD THE EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE AND
  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION’S RECOMMENDATION TO DENY THE
  REQUEST TO HOST A MOUNTED SHOOTING EVENT AT ERNIE HOWLETT
  PARK

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

PUBLIC HEARINGS (7:30 P.M.)

A.  ORDINANCE NO. 727 – AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY OF ROLLING HILLS ESTATES,
  CALIFORNIA AMENDING SECTION 16.04.070 OF THE ROLLING HILLS ESTATES
  MUNICIPAL CODE PERTAINING TO REPEAL OF THE COUNTY SUBDIVISION CODE
  SECTION APPLICABLE TO DURATION OF APPROVALS FOR LEASE PROJECTS

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  6
SEPTEMBER 10, 2019
   Recommendation: That the City Council: 1) Open the public hearing; 2) Take Public
  Testimony; 3) Discuss Ordinance No. 727; 4) Find that the proposed ordinance is exempt
  from the provisions of the California Environmental Quality Act, per Sections 15060(c)(2)
  and 15061(b)(3); 5) Approve for introduction, Ordinance 727 to amend and restate section
  16.04.070 of the Rolling Hills Estates Municipal Code pertaining to repeal of the County
  subdivision code section applicable to duration of approvals for lease projects; and 6)
  Continue the public hearing for second reading and adoption, to the next City Council
  meeting of September 24, 2019.

  Planning Manager Naughton provided a staff report (as per the agenda material) and read
  the full title of the ordinance.

  In response to COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN, Planning Manager Naughton confirmed
  that there is no provision for approval of lease duration upon subdivision.

  CITY ATTORNEY DAVIS further noted that the City does not approve leases of
  subdivisions.

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by, MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL OPEN THE PUBLIC HEARING AND TAKE PUBLIC
  TESTIMONY ORDINANCE NO. 727

  Hearing no objection, MAYOR MITCHELL so ordered and called for public testimony. There
  being no members of the public present to provide public testimony, she asked for any
  additional comments from the City Council.

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by, COUNCIL MEMBER
  ZUCKERMAN

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL FIND THAT THE PROPOSED ORDINANCE IS
  EXEMPT FROM THE PROVISIONS OF THE CALIFORNIA ENVIRONMENTAL
  QUALITY ACT, PER SECTIONS 15060(C)(2) AND 15061(B)(3); INTRODUCE
  ORDINANCE 727 FOR FIRST READING BY TITLE ONLY AND CONTINUE THE
  PUBLIC HEARING TO THE NEXT CITY COUNCIL MEETING SCHEDULE FOR
  SEPTEMBER 24, 2019 FOR SECOND READING AND ADOPTION OF THE
  ORDINANCE.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

NEW BUSINESS (CONTINUED)

D.  OVERVIEW OF REGIONAL HOUSING NEEDS ASSESSMENT NUMBERS

  Recommendation: That the City Council receive and file the report; and provide staff with
  feedback on the proposed RHNA allocation methodology options.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  7
SEPTEMBER 10, 2019
   Planning Manager Naughton provided a PowerPoint overview of the staff report (as per
  the agenda material).

  Lengthy discussion ensued concerning the RHNA numbers, the proposed RHNA
  allocation methodology options and their potential impacts on the community. Planning
  Manager Naughton provided further clarification on the proposed methodology options.

  MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ moved, seconded by, COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL RECEIVE AND FILE THE REPORT

  Hearing no objection, MAYOR MITCHELL so ordered.

OLD BUSINESS

A.  REVIEW AND APPROVAL OF LANDSCAPE MAINTENANCE SERVICES AGREEMENT

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve the updated Landscape Maintenance
  Services Agreement with Bennett Landscape in the amount of $297,293 in year one;
  $289,043 in year two; $274,590 in year three; $260,860 in year four; and $246,796 in
  year five and adjust the Fiscal Year 2019-20 budget accordingly.

  Maintenance Superintendent Goldsmith provided a staff report (as per the agenda
  material).

  City Attorney Davis provided an overview of the updated agreement.

  City Manager Grammer noted that the staff has determined that the City will be able to
  use a portion of its $180,000 annual allocation of Measure W (Clean Safe Water Program)
  funds to offset the increased cost of the contract because it promotes the objectives of
  the measure by removing herbicide pollutants from stormwater runoff.

  Assistant City Manager Davis clarified that staff is working with Bennett Landscape to
  address the portion of the contract associated with neighborhood entryway maintenance.

  In response to MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ regarding clarification concerning the items
  listed on Appendix 1 – Service Areas, Assistant City Manager Davis noted that there was
  formatting error in the numbering on those pages and staff will correct the error.

  Also in response to MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ regarding the interval of service for the
  service areas called out in the contract, Maintenance Superintendent Goldsmith stated
  that it varies, but it is typically once or twice per month.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  8
SEPTEMBER 10, 2019
   COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by, MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL APPROVE THE UPDATED LANDSCAPE
  MAINTENANCE SERVICES AGREEMENT WITH BENNETT LANDSCAPE IN
  THE AMOUNT OF $297,293 IN YEAR ONE; $289,043 IN YEAR TWO; $274,590
  IN YEAR THREE; $260,860 IN YEAR FOUR; AND $246,796 IN YEAR FIVE AND
  ADJUST THE FISCAL YEAR 2019-20 BUDGET ACCORDINGLY.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan and Zuckerman

CITY ATTORNEY ITEMS

NONE.

CITY COUNCIL/REGIONAL COMMITTEE REPORTS:

MAYOR MITCHELL reported that the SCAQMD recently voted to allow local refineries to continue
the use of MHF with mitigation measures, where hers was a dissenting vote on an 8-3 vote.

MAYOR MITCHELL provided an overview of Los Angeles County Sanitation District’s Clear Water
Tunnel Project.

In response to COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN regarding Sanitation District rates, MAYOR
MITCHELL noted that there will likely be an increase; but at this time, there has not been a vote on
rates.

MAYOR MITCHELL reported that the CPA Board recently approved new rates in coordination with
SCE’s recent rate increase with all but the 100% clean rate below the SCE rates and heard a
presentation from SCE regarding their emergency plans to shut down power when there is high fire
risk. She suggested that the City consider hosting a community event to allow SCE to share its
presentation with the community.

MAYOR MITCHELL reminded the community that the City Celebration is scheduled for Saturday,
September 21 and encouraged attendance.

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF informed the COUNCIL of the following upcoming events: Palos
Verdes Peninsula Chamber of Commerce Legislative Forum & Luncheon on Friday, October 11
and Peninsula Education Foundation’s State of the School District on Wednesday, October 2.

MAYOR AND COUNCIL ITEMS:

  This item provides the opportunity for Members of the City Council to request information on currently
  pending projects and/or issues of public concern, direct that an item be agendized for future
  consideration and/or make announcements of interest to the public.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  9
SEPTEMBER 10, 2019
 A.  PRESENTATION: 2019 CHINESE PEOPLE’S ASSOCIATION FOR FRIENDSHIP WITH
  FOREIGN COUNTRIES CULTURAL EXCHANGE DELEGATION (MAYOR MITCHELL)

  MAYOR MITCHELL provided an overview of her cultural exchange trip to China hosted
  and sponsored by the Sino-American Friendship Association and the Chinese People’s
  Association for Friendship with Foreign Countries.

At 9:23 p.m. MAYOR MITCHELL adjourned the open session portion of the meeting and City
Council recessed into closed session in the Conference Room at City Hall.

CLOSED SESSION

A.  PUBLIC EMPLOYEE PERFORMANCE EVALUATION
  Government Code Section 54957
  Title: City Manager (Quarterly Evaluation)

  NO REPORTABLE ACTION

B.  CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL – EXISTING LITIGATION
  Government Code Section 54956.9(d)(1)
  Los Angeles Superior Court Case No. 19TRCV00130; Dr. Hendrik Baars, D.D.S. v.
  SRE DCM PV, LLC; City of Rolling Hills Estates

  NO REPORTABLE ACTION

ADJOURNMENT

At 10:15 p.m. MAYOR MITCHELL adjourned the City Council meeting to the next regular City
Council meeting scheduled to be held on Tuesday, September 24, 2019 at 7:00 p.m. in the
Council Chamber at Rolling Hills Estates City Hall, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive North, Rolling Hills
Estates, California.

Submitted by,  Approved by,

Heidi Luce  Greg Grammer
City Clerk  City Manager

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  10
SEPTEMBER 10, 2019
